facts.statement: Romerodus fossils date to the Pennsylvanian subperiod and possibly the Early Permian.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Pennsylvanian Possible Early Permian record

facts.statement: The genus Romerodus was described by Rainer Zangerl in 1981.
facts.quote: authority: Zangerl, 1981

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Romerodus is Romerodus orodontus.
facts.quote: type_species: Romerodus orodontus

facts.statement: Romerodus lived during the Carboniferous and possibly the Permian periods in North America.
facts.quote: It is known from the Carboniferous and possibly Permian periods of North America

facts.statement: The only named species, R. orodontus, was found in organic shale deposits in Nebraska, USA.
facts.quote: the only named species, R. orodontus, was discovered in organic shale deposits in the U.S. state of Nebraska

facts.statement: Romerodus is now classified as a holocephalan, a group today represented only by chimaeras.
facts.quote: they are now regarded as holocephalans, a diverse subclass which is today only represented by chimaeras

facts.statement: Romerodus lived in deep marine waters and was adapted as a pelagic carnivore.
facts.quote: It inhabited deep-water marine environments, and like its relatives shows adaptations associated with life as a pelagic carnivore

facts.statement: The largest known Romerodus reached approximately 50 cm in total length.
facts.quote: the largest known Romerodus were approximately 50 cm in total length

facts.statement: Romerodus orodontus was named and described in 1981 by Rainer Zangerl from multiple crushed but well-preserved body fossils.
facts.quote: Romerodus orodontus was named and described in 1981 by paleontologist Rainer Zangerl based on multiple crushed (but otherwise well-preserved) body fossils

facts.statement: All described Romerodus specimens come from the Hansen Quarry in Sarpy County, Nebraska.
facts.quote: All described specimens originated from the Hansen Quarry, which is located in Sarpy County, Nebraska

facts.statement: The incomplete articulated specimen FMNH PF 8522 from the Stark Shale is the holotype of Romerodus orodontus.
facts.quote: The incomplete but articulated specimen FMNH PF 8522 from the Stark Shale is designated as the holotype of the genus and species

facts.statement: Isolated teeth possibly belonging to Romerodus have been found in the Early Permian Phosphoria Formation in Grand Teton and Yellowstone national parks.
facts.quote: Isolated teeth referred to as "cf. Romerodus sp." have been identified from the Early Permian Phosphoria Formation, in exposed limestone deposits in what are now Grand Teton and Yellowstone national parks

facts.statement: The maximum stated total length of R. orodontus is approximately 50 cm (20 inches).
facts.quote: The maximum total length of R. orodontus is stated to be approximately 50 cm (20 in) in its description

facts.statement: A specimen of indeterminate species in the René Kindlimann collection measures 56 cm (22 inches) in length.
facts.quote: although a specimen of indeterminate species in the collection of René Kindlimann has been measured at 56 cm (22 in) in length

facts.statement: Most of Romerodus' cartilaginous skeleton was calcified, except for the vertebral centra and dorsal fin radials.
facts.quote: Many elements of Romerodus' cartilaginous skeleton were calcified, with the exceptions of the vertebral centra and the radials of the dorsal fin

facts.statement: The single dorsal fin was supported by fused basal cartilage and positioned above the pectoral girdle.
facts.quote: The single dorsal fin was supported by a plate of fused basal cartilage and was positioned above the pectoral girdle

facts.statement: R. orodontus had broad, flattened, overlapping pavement-like teeth.
facts.quote: the teeth of R. orodontus formed a pavement-like dentition (broad, flattened, and overlapping)

facts.statement: Romerodus had a whorl of teeth along the midline of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Romerodus bore a whorl of teeth along the midline, or symphysis, of the lower jaw

facts.statement: The tooth whorl on the lower jaw of R. orodontus was about 25% of the skull's length.
facts.quote: The whorl-bearing portion of the jaw in R. orodontus was roughly 25% of the length of the skull

facts.statement: Findings suggest Romerodus belongs to the holocephalan lineage distantly related to living chimaeras.
facts.quote: Subsequent findings, however, strongly suggest that the order Eugeneodontiformes, to which Romerodus belongs, are a lineage of holocephalan fish distantly related to living chimaeras

facts.statement: It is debated whether eugeneodonts' shark-like morphology was due to shared ecology rather than direct ancestry with sharks.
facts.quote: Despite their evolutionary proximity to chimaeras, eugeneodonts converged on a similar body and tooth morphology to sharks due to shared ecology

facts.statement: Romerodus fossils from the type specimen were found in the Stark Shale, which was a marine depositional environment.
facts.quote: The Stark Shale, where the type specimen of R. orodontus originated, is believed to have been a marine depositional environment.

facts.statement: During the Late Carboniferous, the area now known as Nebraska was part of the Late Pennsylvanian Midcontinent Sea, a deep inland sea rich in phosphates and organic material.
facts.quote: During the Late Carboniferous, Nebraska was part of the Late Pennsylvanian Midcontinent Sea; a deep, inland sea which was rich in phosphates and organic material.

facts.statement: The genus Romerodus was named by Zangerl in 1981.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Romerodus (genus), Zangerl 1981

facts.statement: Romerodus belongs to the family Caseodontidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Caseodontidae

facts.statement: Romerodus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
facts.quote: Class: Chondrichthyes

facts.statement: Romerodus lived during the Kasimovian stage, between 307 and 303.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kasimovian to Kasimovian (307 to 303.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Romerodus is considered an active, nektonic carnivore and a very powerful swimmer.
facts.quote: In life Romerodus was, as has been proposed for all eugeneodonts, an active, nektonic carnivore, and it is assumed to have been a very powerful swimmer.

facts.statement: Scaling Romerodus's proportions suggests the largest Helicoprion individuals may have reached 7 to 11 meters in length, though this estimate depends on the assumption that both species shared similar ecology and phylogeny.
facts.quote: Directly scaling the cranial and postcranial proportions of Romerodus and its close relatives indicates the largest known Helicoprion individuals may have been between 7 to 11 m in length, although such estimates rely on the notion that both fish were close in ecology and phylogenetic position.

facts.statement: A life-sized replica of Helicoprion davidsii displayed at the Idaho Museum of Natural History used the body proportions and anatomy of caseodonts like Romerodus as a model.
facts.quote: The Idaho Museum of Natural History displayed murals and a life-sized replica of Helicoprion davidsii, which featured body proportions and anatomy based on caseodonts such as Romerodus.
